E047-01.notes: Colon correctly introduces the appositive explanation of 'approach'. B: semicolon followed by fragment 'a lens that would...'. C: creates fragment 'A lens that would bend...'. D: comma splice ('approach, it was a lens'). No second defensible option.

E047-02.notes: Redundancy. 'heavy in weight' (A), 'heavy and weighty' (B), 'heavy, extremely so in weight' (D) are all redundant/wordy. C is concise and parallel with 'difficult to cast'.

E047-03.notes: Comparative 'lighter than'. A/B use 'then' (time word); B also adds a faulty 'that of'. C 'lighter as' is unidiomatic.

E047-04.notes: Modifier 'Arranged in rings around a central lens' must attach to 'each prism'. B makes Fresnel the one arranged in rings; C attaches it to 'there' and shifts to a single prism (and 'there was a prism that bent...' loses the 'each' distribution); D attaches it to 'the job' and is wordy. Only A is clear.

flags.note: Factual check: Cordouan does stand on a rocky islet/plateau at the mouth of the Gironde estuary in southwestern France - accurate. B's phrasing 'unrelated to the essay's focus' is slightly strong (the lighthouse is mentioned), but it clearly beats the alternatives; A falsely claims the sentence explains why Cordouan was chosen, C falsely ties it to visibility range, D claims a contradiction that does not exist.

E047-05.notes: Irrelevant setting detail interrupts the move from installation to 'The improvement was dramatic.'

flags.note: 'For instance' is the only non-contrast option and fits (sentence 10 illustrates the dramatic improvement), though some students may expect an 'omit the transition' choice. Single best answer still clear; A, B, D all signal contrast/replacement that is illogical.

E047-06.notes: Sentence 10 exemplifies sentence 9's claim; However/Nevertheless/Instead all wrongly signal contrast.

E047-07.notes: Plural subject 'lenses' rules out A ('has'), C ('was'), D ('is'). 'had been installed' agrees and fits the past narrative frame ('Within a few decades' of 1823) alongside 'was chosen'. Only plural-compatible option.

E047-08.notes: Possessive 'its' referring to 'each lighthouse's lens' / lighthouse. A = 'it is'; B nonstandard; C plural pronoun mismatched with singular 'each lighthouse'.

E047-09.notes: The clause establishes Fresnel's expertise in light bending, explaining why he could propose a refracting lens. A (manufacturing), B (soot), D (comparison with other physicists) are not in the clause.

flags.note: 'brighter' in B is an inference (passage says 'one strong horizontal beam' and greater visibility range, not 'brighter' explicitly); reasonable and not a defect. Other options are clearly false: A (no list of lighthouses), C (keepers are a minor detail), D (sentence 6 does explain how the light was directed).

E047-10.notes: Essay shows the problem (heavy lenses/wasteful mirrors) solved by Fresnel's optics.

E047-11.notes: Phrase gives the brand name (Palmer did market the kits as Craft Master - accurate). A: does not explain the sales rise; C: name not given earlier; D: no contradiction. Paint-by-number facts checked: Dan Robbins, Palmer Paint Co. of Detroit, owner Max Klein, Leonardo numbering anecdote, early slow sales and department-store demonstration turnaround, Smithsonian (National Museum of American History) exhibition in 2001 - all consistent with standard accounts.

E047-12.notes: Sequence: Klein doubtful (4) -> early kits sold poorly (5) -> sales improved after demonstration (6) -> millions sold (7). B/C put poor early sales after the improvement; D puts it before the owner's initial doubt, breaking the 'at first' sequence and separating the problem from its resolution less logically. Current placement best.
